note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  - Lower abdominal (lower tummy) pain for 2 days.
  - Feels hot and sweaty.
  - Not triggered by food, medication, or environmental exposure described.
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  - Onset: 2 days ago.
  - Progression: persistent; mild nausea without vomiting; no improvement reported.
- ENT symptoms:
  - Throat swelling/closure sensation: none reported.
  - Voice change/hoarseness: none reported.
  - Dysphagia/odynophagia: none reported.
  - Drooling: none reported.
  - Nasal/ocular symptoms: none reported.
  - Stridor/noisy breathing: none reported.
  - Dyspnea: none reported.
  - Distribution of swelling (lips/tongue/uvula/face): none reported.
  - Ear pain/hearing changes: none reported.
  - Neck pain/swelling: none reported.
- Other relevant symptoms:
  - Mild nausea; no vomiting.
  - Slight pink discoloration noted in urine by patient (patient described “some slight blood in the urine”).
  - Slightly increased urinary frequency; no pain on passing urine (no dysuria).
  - Constipated last week but bowel action now normal; last stool ~2 hours ago.
  - Measured temperature ~37°C about 1 hour prior.
  - No back pain, no recent travel.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  - No prior similar episodes reported.
  - No prior hospitalizations, ED visits, or injection therapies documented.
- Allergies and current medications:
  - Allergy: amoxicillin.
  - Regular medications: none documented.
  - Contraception: patient stated she “had the internal contraceptive implant for one year, now no more” (status per patient).
- Social context:
  - Lives with parents.
  - Does not smoke.
  - Alcohol: drinks approximately one beer, four times per week.
  - Presence of another person during consult: not stated.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution: none stated.
- Airway/breathing descriptors: none stated.
- Mental status and associated features:
  - Patient alert and conversational; reports feeling hot and sweaty.
- Vitals and examination findings:
  - Temperature: ~37°C (measured ~1 hour prior).
  - Other vitals and physical examination findings: Not recorded.
- Presence of another person with the patient: Not recorded.

Assessment:
- Primary clinical impression:
  - Suspected urinary tract infection (lower abdominal pain, reported hematuria/pink urine, mild fever, increased urinary frequency).
  - No evidence of ENT pathology or upper airway/allergic reaction on history—no throat symptoms, voice change, respiratory compromise, or facial/lip/tongue swelling reported.
- Justification:
  - Lower abdominal pain for 2 days with reported pink urine and mild fever supports possible UTI.
  - Absence of ENT/airway symptoms on history argues against acute ENT emergency.
- Conflict noted:
  - Contraceptive implant status is ambiguous in phrasing (“had … for one year, now no more”) — potential conflict/uncertainty about current contraceptive status.

Plan:
- Immediate actions taken/advised:
  - Offer and patient agreed to a short course of antibiotics to be sent to allocated pharmacy.
  - Antibiotic instruction per clinician: take twice daily for 3 days. (Medication name not documented.)
  - Start antibiotic as soon as received.
- Specific instructions provided to patient:
  - If pain worsens, if you develop a high temperature, back pain, new symptoms, or recurrence of the problem — contact the service straightaway.
  - If symptoms do not improve or worsen, a face-to-face assessment may be required.
- Escalation criteria / red flags (as stated):
  - Worsening pain.
  - High temperature (fever).
  - Development of back pain.
  - New or worsening symptoms.
- Follow-up:
  - Re-contact clinician/service if symptoms worsen or do not improve; consider face-to-face examination if indicated.
  - No ENT or allergy follow-up required based on current history.
- Medication documentation:
  - Antibiotic prescribed — name not documented; regimen stated as twice daily for 3 days.
- COVID-19 vaccine suitability: not discussed.
- Emergency contact instructions exactly as stated in transcript:
  - “If the pain is getting worse, or you have a high temperature or back pain or develop any new symptoms, … we should speak to you again, because we might need to see you face-to-face for an examination.”
  - “If your pain’s getting worse, … or you’ve got new symptoms, just contact us straightaway, or if you’re getting a recurrence of the same problem again.”
  
Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Antibiotic name, dose, route not documented.
  - Urine dipstick/urinalysis and/or urine culture results not documented or performed.
  - Comprehensive vital signs (HR, BP, RR, O2 saturation) not recorded.
  - Pregnancy status/last menstrual/pregnancy test not documented (reproductive-aged patient).
  - Abdominal and pelvic examination findings not available (no face-to-face exam documented).
  - Clear documentation of contraceptive implant current status (ambiguous).
  - No plan documented for follow-up testing or sexual/reproductive counseling if indicated.
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - Ambiguous statement regarding contraceptive implant (“had … for one year, now no more”) — unclear whether currently present or removed.
- Transcript quality:
  - Overall consult audio/transcript clear with minor brief inaudible/hesitant phrases; clinician and patient statements identifiable.
